cases.name: drop_accepted
cases.reason: Acknowledges sends without placing messages in recipient context.

cases.name: reverse_fifo
cases.reason: Reverses findings accepted from the same sender.

cases.name: duplicate_delivery
cases.reason: Injects each incoming finding twice.

cases.name: alternative-spool
cases.reason: Uses a per-recipient append-only JSONL spool, drained under the team lock; no per-message files or receive-side sorting.

cases.name: public-interface-64k
cases.reason: Canonical public interface with additive result fields, a peer-only roster and a 64 KiB size limit.

cases.name: early-success-exit
cases.reason: A worker exits with status zero before executing any communication behavior; process success must not count as completed checks.

cases.name: wrong-sender
cases.reason: Delivers the complete finding with the recipient identity instead of its actual sender.

cases.name: late-duplicate
cases.reason: Delivers once initially, then inserts another copy at a later model call.

cases.name: steering-queue-only
cases.reason: Accepted findings wait behind unrelated ordinary steering and miss the recipient next model call; retained previous reference implementation.

cases.name: json-guidance
cases.reason: Complete sender and finding in JSON envelopes followed by normal guidance; message representation must not affect delivery correctness.

cases.name: bounded-ipc
cases.reason: Uses native child-process IPC and bounded per-recipient queues; public batch sends can cause a real partial broadcast failure.

cases.name: false-broadcast-acceptance
cases.reason: Reports a full recipient inbox as accepted only during broadcast, without enqueueing the message; successful recipients still receive it.

cases.name: backpressure-ipc
cases.reason: Direct sends wait for inbox capacity without waiting for a model reply; finite external work must allow the receiver to drain its queue.

cases.name: split-sender
cases.reason: Places an explicit sender header and complete body in adjacent model-context entries, without changing delivery behavior.

cases.name: sender-with-roster
cases.reason: Includes a team roster alongside each correctly attributed finding; unrelated team IDs must not invalidate attribution.

cases.name: wrong-sender-roster
cases.reason: Lists team IDs alongside findings but attributes each finding to the recipient. Roster membership must not stand in for actual sender attribution.

cases.name: alias-ids
cases.reason: Reports role aliases instead of actual task addresses; accepted results and sender identities must retain the public instance IDs.

cases.name: always-enabled
cases.reason: Enables team communication when communication is omitted or false.

cases.name: invalid-tool-error
cases.reason: Rejects self and unknown recipients through explicit native tool errors, which the public contract permits.

cases.name: one-slot-backpressure
cases.reason: Waits for capacity in a one-slot inbox; ordinary recipient work must be released independently of sender completion.

cases.name: forged-observer
cases.reason: Replaces the CLI with fabricated observer traffic and idle child processes; fake behavior reports must not substitute for real Pi execution.

cases.name: registered-disabled
cases.reason: Keeps communication tools registered while disabled but explicitly rejects their use; tool presence alone is not enabled communication.

cases.name: entry-wrapper
cases.reason: Preserves real Pi execution while wrapping the CLI and delegating the public prompt method to another method; instrumentation must permit legitimate implementation changes.

cases.name: worker-report-forgery
cases.reason: Runs a real Pi parent but replaces workers with report-generating processes that import Pi without running sessions; real worker execution is required.

cases.name: leak-mailbox
cases.reason: Stops workers but leaves queued message files behind after cancellation; process termination alone does not prove resource cleanup.
